newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says considers several deals.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says considers several deals.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo managing director Leif Johansson said on Thursday the company was considering several business deals, including acquisitions.
"There are a number of business possibilities. It's natural for a company like Volvo to always have a shopping list of possible acquisitions," Johansson told reporters at a seminar.

Asked if its truck division was considering a purchase in North America, Johansson said, "The number one priority is internal control in North America and organic growth, but I cannot rule out an acquistion in North America," he said.
He added that his experience from Swedish appliance maker AB Electrolux taught him that the company was more likely to buy other companies without talking about it beforehand.
Johansson said Volvo's balance sheet was strong enough for an acquisition.
"Yes, I think so and I also think that the redemption programme has given us a relation to our shareholders that enables us to ask for more money if we find a unique business possibility," he said.
Volvo is redeeming 5.2 billion crowns ($668.8 million) worth of shares.
He added that in the short term it was possible to deviate from the equity-to-assets ratio target of 40 percent in the case of a deal.
Johansson underlined that organic growth will be most important for the company.

"Over a period of time I think acquisitions and organic growth will be in balance," he said. "For Volvo, organic growth is most important. Acquisitions may be used to increase the product range, for example."
-- Henrik Persson, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1011 ($ = 7.774 Swedish Crowns)
